item.content:encoded:
Pine Labs Sees Profits Swell

Pine Labs put up a strong show in Q2 FY27. Buoyed by broad-based improvement across its core verticals and rising margins, the fintech major’s revenue growth hit a five-quarter high during the quarter while its net profit skyrocketed six-fold. 

Here’s the breakdown of Pine Labs’ Q2 numbers: 

  • Net profit surged over 6X YoY to ₹38.6 Cr
  • Operating revenue rose 24% YoY to ₹806.2 Cr
  • Total expenses rose 16% YoY to ₹770.4 Cr
  • Adjusted EBITDA rose 27% YoY to ₹215.5 Cr

Double Growth Engine: The startup’s Q2 performance reflected higher GTV, new products, an expanding merchant ecosystem and double-digit growth across its core digital infrastructure and issuing platform verticals. In addition, increased operating leverage outpaced expense growth, further strengthening cash flows. 

The company also continued to deepen its monetisation capabilities through new value-added services and AI-led credit underwriting tools that process over 1 Lakh loans monthly.

The MDR Boost: Pine Labs sees a “meaningful upside” from the proposal to re-introduce merchant discount rate on UPI transactions above ₹2,000. Given that enterprise merchants drive a substantial share of its volume, the company plans to aggressively deploy additional soundbox devices to capture a bigger chunk of merchant wallet share.

Around The World: International markets are also becoming a bigger part of Pine Labs’ business, contributing 15% of its top line in Q2. The company now operates across more than 22 markets and is seeing strong momentum in Southeast Asia, where revenue and digital checkout points expanded rapidly in the quarter. While the UAE business crossed a meaningful daily transaction milestone, the company is also building presence in the Philippines and Singapore. 

These markets give Pine Labs a broader runway beyond India and reduce dependence on any single regulatory environment. With its underlying businesses compounding, here’s a closer look at Pine Labs performed in Q2 FY27…

From The Editor’s Desk

Ace Blend Bags $9.9 Mn

  • The D2C nutrition brand has raised about ₹95 Cr in its Series A2 round led by 3one4 Capital to invest in clinical trials, R&D, supply chain improvements and testing of its products.
  • Founded in 2018, Ace Blend offers supplements across heart health, brain health, sleep, gut health and immunity. Its portfolio comprises around 14 SKUs. It is targeting ₹250-300 Cr in annual recurring revenue over the next 12-18 months.
  • Ace Blend operates in the broader Indian dietary supplements market, which is being driven by growing consumer demand, user awareness and the rise of preventive healthcare. The space is projected to become a $12 Bn opportunity by 2033.

Shadowfax’s Q2 Profit Run

  • The listed logistics major’s net profit surged over 5X YoY to ₹68 Cr in Q2 FY27, while operating revenue jumped 57% YoY to a record ₹1,537.7 Cr. Shadowfax’s adjusted EBITDA also rose 177% YoY to ₹77 Cr, with margins expanding to 5% from 2.8%.
  • On the operational front, the platform delivered 27.1 Cr orders across its express parcel and hyperlocal businesses in Q2. Its 360 platform also crossed 6,700 transacting sellers within two quarters of launch.
  • Founded in 2015, Shadowfax provides last-mile delivery services to ecommerce platforms and D2C brands. The company listed on the stock exchanges in January this year following its bumper ₹1,907 Cr IPO.

Venttup Raises $3 Mn

  • The precision manufacturing startup has raised the funding in its Pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter and Unicorn India Ventures to scale hiring, its rapid prototyping infrastructure and AI-led sourcing.
  • Founded in 2021, Venttup combines in-house engineering with its network of manufacturing partners to support component development, testing, and production. It claims to have grown its revenue to ₹10 Cr in FY26.
  • On the operational front, the startup added more than 15 blue-chip customers over the past 12 months and built an approximately ₹30 Cr business opportunity pipeline across new energy, mobility, and smart infrastructure.

Bijnis Rebrands As Zorit

  • The B2B ecommerce startup has rebranded as Zorit and raised ₹27 Cr in a funding round led by Sparrow Capital. Zorit now plans to double down on an inventory-led quick commerce model for offline retailers and expand its product assortment.
  • Founded in 2015, Bijnis initially operated an online marketplace that connected manufacturers with retailers. It pivoted to an inventory-led B2B quick commerce model in late 2024. As Bijnis, the startup had raised over $43 Mn.
  • In its new avatar, the startup allows retailers to source products within 60 minutes. Zorit currently claims to operate 12 dark stores across 12 cities and claims to have reached ₹120 Cr in annualised sales. Nearly half of its stores have achieved break-even.

Crypto Startups Under ED Lens

  • The Enforcement Directorate has launched a probe into alleged forex violations by crypto platforms Mudrex, Saber.money and Instadapp. The investigation involves alleged unauthorised cross-border fund transfers worth more than ₹4,940 Cr.
  • The agency said its Bengaluru Zonal Office conducted searches at three premises in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh on October 27. 
  • The investigations centre on the alleged use of cryptocurrencies, particularly stablecoins such as USDT and USDC, to facilitate cross-border money transfers outside authorised channels.

Can Physioplus’ AI Stack Track India’s Recovery Journey?

Physiotherapy often breaks down between appointments. While patients struggle to follow exercises, therapists lack real-time visibility into progress. To solve this, Physioplus is building a digital layer that keeps assessment and recovery tracking connected beyond the clinic.

A Digital Coach: Founded in 2022, Physioplus’ AI-powered platform helps patients discover physiotherapists, book consultations, request home visits and receive support for chronic pain and post-surgery rehabilitation. The platform is designed to make access more convenient while helping clinicians understand a patient’s history before treatment begins.

The Rehabilitation Stack: For practitioners, Physioplus combines digital practice management, patient records, clinical assessments, documentation and tech-enabled monitoring. Its monitoring layer also supports home-based rehabilitation by capturing exercise adherence, pain changes and functional progress over time. 

Growing Steadily: Physioplus claims to have so far onboarded over 1,000 patients. It is now focusing on scaling product development, expanding its physiotherapist network and fueling growth across India. With the homegrown digital health and rehabilitation market projected to become a $14.8 Bn opportunity by 2033, can Physioplus make physiotherapy more measurable and consistent beyond the clinic?

item.title: Exclusive: Smylo In Talks To Raise ₹30 Cr To Expand Cat Food Portfolio
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: D2C cat food startup Smylo is in advanced talks to raise around ₹30 Cr (about $3.2 Mn) in a mix…
item.content:encoded:
D2C cat food startup Smylo is in advanced talks to raise around ₹30 Cr (about $3.2 Mn) in a mix of equity and debt, sources told Inc42.

The proposed round is likely to bring a new venture capital firm onto Smylo’s cap table, with existing backer DSG Consumer Partners also looking to invest further, the sources added.

While the split between equity and debt could not be ascertained, the sources said equity would account for the majority of the round.

Smylo is likely to use the fresh capital for new product launches, R&D, and setting up a manufacturing facility.

Inc42 has reached out to Smylo for comment. The story will be updated on receiving a response.

Founded in 2024 by former Titan Capital executives Abhishek Agrawal and Kartikeya Gupta, Smylo offers cat food that it claims is preservative-free, high in protein, and made from fresh meat.

Its portfolio includes wet food, dry food, and broths for kittens and adult cats. Besides its website, the startup sells through ecommerce marketplaces and quick commerce platforms such as Blinkit and Zepto.

In an interaction with Inc42 in February, the founders said Smylo was clocking average monthly sales of ₹50–55 Lakh. Its website and ecommerce channels contributed about 80% of revenue, with quick commerce accounting for the remainder.  

At the time, the startup had raised smaller rounds before securing investment during its appearance on Shark Tank India in early 2026. However, the startup did not disclose the total funding raised. 

The development comes amid continued investment in India’s pet care market, with startups across food, supplies, and healthcare raising capital to expand their operations.

In September, D2C pet food startup Lickicious raised ₹19 Cr through a mix of equity and debt in a round led by Prath Ventures. It planned to use the capital to expand manufacturing, strengthen R&D, and widen its product range and sales channels.

Pet care marketplace Supertails raised $30 Mn in a Series C round in February to expand its pet clinic network and quick commerce infrastructure. 

Investor interest is being driven by India’s growing pet care market, with rising pet ownership and higher spending on pet nutrition and healthcare.

India’s pet care market is estimated to be worth $3.6 Bn in 2024 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 20% to reach $24.8 Bn by 2032, according to IBEF.

item.title: Nasscom Seeks Deferment Of New GST Rules For Ecommerce Deliveries To Jan 2027
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: Industry body Nasscom has urged the finance ministry to defer the implementation of the revised GST rules for ecommerce delivery…
item.content:encoded:
Industry body Nasscom has urged the finance ministry to defer the implementation of the revised GST rules for ecommerce delivery services to January 2027. 

In a representation submitted to the ministry on October 28, the industry body sought an adequate transition period for marketplaces to overhaul their technology, accounting and compliance systems in line with the new regime.

It also urged the ministry to conduct consultations with ecommerce operators, logistics providers and other businesses impacted by the new norms. 

It is pertinent to note that the GST rules were notified on October 27 and are scheduled to take effect on November 1, leaving companies only a few days to comply. The changes follow recommendations made by the 57th GST Council on October 8. 

The new norms introduce a 5% GST rate without input tax credit (ITC) for specified delivery services. The rules also revised the scope of services for which ecommerce operators must discharge tax liability.

“While these changes aim to bring greater consistency to GST treatment, their implementation would require significant adjustments across the ecommerce and logistics ecosystem,” Nasscom said.

Citing its rationale, Nasscom said that implementing the new framework would require changes to enterprise resource planning (ERP) configurations, invoicing, tax calculations, input tax credit treatment and GST compliance processes. The industry body also noted that marketplaces would need to examine the notified provisions, assess how they apply to different operating models and test their systems before deployment.

Based on industry assessments, Nasscom requested a January 1 implementation date to complete the necessary adjustments.

The association also called for industry-wide consultation to clarify requirements and address implementation challenges, arguing that coordinated preparation would help prevent avoidable disruptions.

At the heart of the development is the revised tax framework, which reduces GST on specified delivery services from 18% to 5% but also removes the eligibility for ITC. This means impacted service providers cannot offset eligible GST paid on business inputs against their output tax liability.

As such, a lower headline rate does not necessarily translate into an equivalent reduction in operating costs or customer delivery charges. The impact will depend on each business’s structure and input tax position.

The notified wording also replaces “local delivery” with “delivery services, other than postal and courier services”, broadening the description beyond local deliveries.

With this, the immediate question for ecommerce platforms is whether the government will extend the deadline and give businesses more time to align their systems with the new regime. Will the finance ministry give in? Only time will tell.

item.title: Let’s Game Now Bags ₹30 Cr To Organise More Esports Tournaments
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: The Indian gaming industry has been forced to rethink its growth strategy after the government banned real money gaming (RMG)…
item.content:encoded:
The Indian gaming industry has been forced to rethink its growth strategy after the government banned real money gaming (RMG) in 2025, a major revenue stream for the industry till then.

In trying to regain footing, many gaming startups are aggressively doubling down on adjacent businesses — esports, tournaments and brand-led gaming. Let’s Game Now also wants to tap this opportunity by building a franchise-based gaming league that brings together competitive gaming, sports and entertainment.

To fuel this ambition, the Bengaluru-based gaming and esports company has raised ₹30 Cr in an investment round led by industrialist Anand Mahindra, Bestvantage Investments and an undisclosed UAE-based family office

The funding will be used to accelerate the development of the Indian Super Gaming League (ISGL), the company’s proposed gaming and entertainment property. 

Founded in 2018 by Santanu Basu, Let’s Game Now is an Indian esports platform that connects brands with gamers. The startup also provides live broadcasting services across South Asia and Southeast Asia and organises online competitions and offline events.

The gaming platform claims to have so far organised more than 2,000 events and serves over 30 clients. It also has a presence in 18 countries and claims to have a total reach of over 50 Mn viewers.

Building A Franchise-Based Gaming League

The Indian Super Gaming League sits at the centre of Let’s Game Now’s expansion plans. The startup aims to bring competitive gaming, sports, entertainment and technology together through a franchise-based format.

The model offers an opportunity to build a recurring gaming property around teams, players and fans, rather than relying solely on individual tournaments and brand-led events.

Mahindra’s backing brings experience from the sports and business ecosystem, including associations with properties such as the Pro Kabaddi League and Chess League.

However, the commercial viability of ISGL will depend on its ability to attract franchise owners, sponsors, broadcasting partners and a consistent audience. The startup has not disclosed the league’s launch timeline, franchise structure, expected revenue or monetisation strategy.

Let’s Game Now’s Commercial Bet

India’s gaming market is valued at nearly $3.8 Bn and is projected to reach $9.2 Bn by FY29. The country is home to an estimated 59.1 Cr gamers.

For Let’s Game Now, the opportunity lies in converting this audience into a commercially viable ecosystem for teams, sponsors, broadcasters and other partners.

The startup claims it has built a community of over 14 Lakh members and a grassroots network spanning more than 400 colleges across 80 cities. Its reach also includes over 7 Lakh students, supported by 20+ events and 30+ college club partnerships.

This network could help the startup acquire participants and audiences for ISGL. Its existing relationships with brands and experience in organising tournaments may also provide a starting point for building commercial partnerships.

However, the startup will need to demonstrate repeat viewership, sponsor demand and a format that can sustain interest across seasons. Its next phase will hinge on three factors:

  • Franchise and sponsorship demand: Whether the league can attract teams, franchise owners and brands willing to commit capital over multiple seasons.
  • Audience monetisation: Whether its existing gaming community can translate into consistent viewership and revenue from sponsorships, media rights and other commercial partnerships.
  • League economics: Whether the revenue generated can cover the costs of organising competitions, running broadcasts, acquiring audiences and maintaining franchise participation.

The ₹30 Cr investment provides capital to advance the league, but Let’s Game Now has not disclosed how much of the funding will go towards league operations, marketing, technology or other business functions.

Inc42 Take: Can Let’s Game Now Build A Scalable Esports Business?

Let’s Game Now is looking to build on India’s large gaming audience by creating a franchise-based property rather than relying only on individual tournaments and events.

Its existing community, grassroots network and investor backing offer a starting point. However, these are not proof of a sustainable esports business. The key question is whether ISGL can generate recurring commercial demand from the stakeholders while retaining audiences across seasons.

Economics will also matter. League operations, production, marketing and franchise development can require significant spending, while revenue depends on the ability to secure and retain commercial partners.

The real test will be whether it can turn its gaming community into a repeatable commercial property, with consistent viewership and revenue beyond the initial investment.

item.title: Klassroom H1: Profit Jumps 24% YoY To ₹4 Cr, Revenue Up 21%
item.dc:creator: Team Inc42
item.description: BSE SME-listed edtech startup Klassroom reported a net profit of ₹4.8 Cr in the first half (H1) of the fiscal…
item.content:encoded:
BSE SME-listed edtech startup Klassroom reported a net profit of ₹4.8 Cr in the first half (H1) of the fiscal year 2026-27 (FY27), up 23.8% from ₹3.9 Cr in the year-ago period. On a sequential basis, the platform’s bottom line improved 31.6% from ₹3.6 Cr in H2 FY26.

The profits came as operating revenue for the period under review rose 21.1% to ₹14.9 Cr compared to ₹12.3 Cr in H1 FY26. The top line also zoomed nearly 39% from ₹10.7 Cr in the six month period ended March 2026.

Including other income of ₹12.4 Lakh, Klassroom’s total income for H1 FY27 stood at ₹15 Cr.

In line with the top line, the listed company’s total expenses also saw a sharp jump. Klassroom also incurred additional tax expenses of ₹1.6 Cr in H1 FY27, up 68.2% from ₹96.4 Lakhs in the year-ago period. 

Separately, in a filing with the exchanges, Klassroom also said that its board has approved the appointment of ND Associates’ Neeta Desai as the secretarial auditor of the company for a period of five years till FY31. The board also cleared a proposal to appoint Pratik Gamot as the internal auditor of the Company for FY27.

The financials come more than two months after Fusion Klassroom Edutech made a bumper listing on the BSE SME platform. Shares of the edtech platform listed at ₹170, a premium of 6.92% to the issue price of ₹159. 

The public issue comprised a fresh issue of up to 19.89 Lakh shares and an offer for sale (OFS) component of up to 4.66 Lakh shares. The IPO was subscribed 1.46X. Klassroom had set a price band of ₹151 to ₹159 for the issue, seeking a valuation of ₹148.1 Cr at the upper end of its spectrum.

Zooming Into Klassroom’s H1 Expenses

Klassroom’s total expenses rose 14.4% to ₹8.6 Cr in H1 FY27 as against ₹7.5 Cr in the year-ago period. Here is how the company spent during the period under review:

Other Expenses: This was the biggest cost centre for the company. Klassroom spent ₹3.4 Cr under this bucket in the six month period ended September 2026, up 34.8% from ₹2.5 Cr in H1 FY26. The edtech platform did not give a breakdown of these expenses. 

Employee Benefit Expenses: The edtech platform incurred an expenditure of nearly ₹80 Lakh under this header in H1 FY27 compared to ₹57.1 Lakh in the year ago period. 

Purchase Of Stock-In Trade: Klassroom also spent ₹64 Lakh to buy finished goods in the period under review. This was more than 70% lower than ₹2.1 Cr in H1 FY26.

Operating Expenses: Expenditure under this bucket declined 76.9% to ₹51.7 Lakh in H1 FY27 as against ₹2.2 Cr in the year ago period. 

Shares of Klassroom closed Thursday’s trading session 4.94% higher at ₹170 on the BSE.

item.title: ED Probes Unauthorised Cross-Border Crypto Transfers Worth ₹4,940 Cr
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has launched investigations into alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) involving crypto platforms…
item.content:encoded:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has launched investigations into alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) involving crypto platforms Mudrex and Saber.money, as well as decentralised finance (DeFi) protocol Instadapp and its associated platform Fluid, over alleged unauthorised cross-border fund transfers worth more than ₹4,940 Cr.

The agency said its Bengaluru Zonal Office conducted searches at three premises in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh on October 27 under Section 37 of FEMA, 1999.

The investigations centre on the alleged use of cryptocurrencies, particularly stablecoins such as USDT and USDC, to facilitate cross-border money transfers outside authorised channels.

The ED said its preliminary investigation into the Mudrex and Saber.money operations indicated alleged FEMA violations exceeding ₹4,600 Cr. Separately, the agency alleged contraventions amounting to approximately $40 Mn (around ₹380.6 Cr) in the Instadapp/Fluid case.

ED Flags Alleged Unauthorised Transfers Through Crypto Platforms

The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has searched four premises in Bengaluru and Madhya Pradesh as part of an investigation into alleged unauthorised cross-border financial transactions involving cryptocurrency worth more than ₹5,000 Cr.

The agency’s Bengaluru Zonal Office conducted the searches earlier this week on October 27 under the FEMA regulations. In a post on X, the ED said its probe had uncovered the alleged use of shell entities in tax-haven jurisdictions, large over-the-counter (OTC) transactions and foreign payouts through cryptocurrency platforms such as Binance and Bybit. <

It has identified Bengaluru-based RPFAS Technologies Pvt Ltd, which operates  platforms Mudrex and Saber.money, among the entities which allegedly use crypto currencies for unauthorised cross border transactions and trading. 

“The entity is openly advertising instant money transfer across borders using cryptocurrencies despite not being authorised with RBI,” the agency said.

The platforms also allegedly offered crypto on-ramp and off-ramp services, allowing users to convert traditional currencies such as INR, USD and EUR into digital assets and subsequently withdraw the proceeds into bank accounts.

The ED alleged that these services were used to facilitate cross-border transfers through stablecoins, bypassing authorised channels for international remittances.

In a separate investigation, the ED examined Instadapp, a DeFi protocol deployed on the Ethereum blockchain, and its associated platform Fluid. Instadapp provides tools for decentralised finance activities, including lending, borrowing and swapping crypto assets through smart contracts.

The ED alleged that entities associated with the protocol were incorporated in foreign jurisdictions but managed from India. These entities were reportedly registered across jurisdictions including the US, Singapore, the British Virgin Islands and Dubai.

According to the agency, searches and preliminary investigations indicated that some of these entities did not have physical offices or employees at their registered addresses, while their operations were allegedly managed from India.

The ED further alleged that funds received from overseas investors were routed through foreign bank accounts and subsequently transferred to India to meet expenses and other payments.

This is the second such investigation that the agency has revealed in recent months. In June, the ED searched six premises linked to five Bengaluru-based platforms — Transak, Carret, Xpat, Onramp.money and Onmeta — over alleged unauthorised cross-border crypto transfers. 

The agency froze bank accounts holding around ₹6 Cr, alleging the platforms circumvented FEMA by using stablecoins to route remittances outside authorised channels. It said the entities lacked RBI authorisation for such transfers and operated through foreign-registered entities controlled from India.

It is pertinent to note that cryptocurrencies remain unregulated in India, while also attracting a 30% capital gains tax and 1% TDS on every transaction. 

Authorities continue to flag risks in the ecosystem, with the parliamentary standing committee on finance last month classifying the asset class as “high risk” citing rampant money laundering, trafficking, radicalisation and suspicious crypto transaction.

item.title: Bijnis Rebrands As Zorit, Raises ₹27 Cr For B2B Quick Commerce
item.dc:creator: Anne Florentyna
item.description: Delhi-based B2B ecommerce startup Bijnis has rebranded as Zorit and raised  ₹27 Cr in a funding round led by Sparrow…
item.content:encoded:
Delhi-based B2B ecommerce startup Bijnis has rebranded as Zorit and raised  ₹27 Cr in a funding round led by Sparrow Capital, as it doubles down on an inventory-led quick-commerce model for offline retailers.

The round saw participation from existing investors Info Edge and WaterBridge Ventures, Better Capital, and angel investors including Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal, the founders of Shiprocket, Xpressbees CEO Mohit Sardana and Sarthak Misra of SoftBank, as per its press note.

The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its quick commerce infrastructure, expand its product assortment and deepen engagement with retailers across its operating markets.

Founded in 2015 by Siddharth Vij, Chaitanya Rathi, Siddharth Rastogi and Sachin Chauhan, the startup initially built a digital marketplace connecting manufacturers with retailers. It shifted to an inventory-led B2B quick-commerce model in late 2024, stocking products in local dark stores to enable faster replenishment for neighbourhood retailers.

As Bijnis, the startup had raised over $43 Mn, including a $30 Mn funding round. However, the startup ran into severe operational and financial trouble by 2023.

In its new avatar, the startup allows retailers to source products locally stocked dark stores, with delivery in as little as 60 minutes. This compares with the seven-to-eight-day delivery cycles of its earlier online B2B model and the 24–48-hour fulfilment typically offered by local wholesale traders.

Zorit currently claims to operate 12 dark stores across 12 cities and claims to have reached ₹120 Cr in annualised sales. Nearly half of its stores have achieved break-even, including the cost of liquidating unsold inventory, the company said.

The startup said that monthly ordering frequency has increased fivefold compared with its previous model, while retailer retention beyond the sixth month has improved fourfold. 

“Zorit’s quick commerce model has brought a new segment of retailers into digital sourcing, with  nearly 60% having never used an online B2B platform before. Compared with its previous model,  retailer retention beyond month 6 has improved 4X,” cofounder and CEO Siddharth Vij said.

Info Edge wrote off its entire ₹76.6 Cr investment in Bijnis in 2023. The investor cited continuing cash burn, limited cash availability relative to potential liabilities linked to investor buyback obligations, and uncertainty over future fundraising back then.

On the fresh investment, Info Edge Ventures’ partner Kitty Agarwal said, “Zorit’s manufacturer-first approach has now evolved into a powerful quick-commerce layer for  small retailers – enabling access to a wide assortment with speed and ease. This has unlocked  incredible frequency and retention among retailers, while simultaneously creating deeper demand  for manufacturers.”

item.title: Spacetech Soonicorn Pixxel Eyes US Expansion With New Subsidiary
item.dc:creator: Gaurav Bagur
item.description: Bengaluru-based Pixxel has set up a new subsidiary in the US, Pixxel Federal, to tap into the US government market…
item.content:encoded:
Bengaluru-based Pixxel has set up a new subsidiary in the US, Pixxel Federal, to tap into the US government market and build on its existing engagements with NASA and the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO). 

The startup, which just raised $100 Mn last month, is now planning to set up an office  around Washington, DC to work more closely with government customers and partners.

The US subsidiary intends to offer earth observation technologies, satellite mission systems and geospatial intelligence to American government agencies across civilian, defence and intelligence sectors. 

“The US government market represents a significant opportunity for Pixxel as we expand our capabilities beyond hyperspectral imaging into advanced sensing technologies, software, and satellite systems,” said the startup’s founder and CEO Awais Ahmed. 

Pixxel executive Allyson Jenkins – previously Vice President, Public Sector – has been appointed CEO of Pixxel Federal. She had already been leading the company’s US government business since joining in January 2025. 

Important to mention that Pixxel recently secured a contract through NASA’s Commercial SmallSat Data Acquisition Programme and a Strategic Commercial Enhancements contract from the NRO. The new subsidiary will build on these relationships to pursue additional federal contracts and strengthen the company’s position in the US space and geospatial intelligence market. 

It will leverage Pixxel’s hyperspectral satellites, Earth intelligence software and satellite mission systems for applications such as camouflage detection, terrain characterisation, critical mineral and rare earth element detection, environmental monitoring and agriculture.

Founded in 2019 by BITS Pilani alumni Ahmed and Kshitij Khandelwal, Pixxel claims to operate the world’s highest-resolution constellation of commercial hyperspectral satellites, which can capture light across a large number of narrow wavelength bands to identify details or changes on the Earth’s surface that conventional imagery may miss. 

Besides its US government contracts, Pixxel has won multiple iDEX challenges in India from the Ministry of Defence and is currently developing a public-private Earth observation satellite constellation under IN-SPACe. The proposed constellation, which is expected to be India’s first of its kind, will comprise 12 satellites carrying different types of imaging sensors.

In September, the startup raised $100 Mn in a Series C round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim, marking the largest single investment round for an Indian spacetech company. 

With the round, Pixxel’s total private funding now is around $195 Mn. Investors like Google, Radical Ventures, growX ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, 360 ONE Asset, are on its cap table.

item.title: Thyrocare Q2 Profit Slips 68% YoY To ₹15 Cr On ₹45 Cr Exceptional Expense
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: PharmEasy-backed Thyrocare’s net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) slumped 68.2% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹15.2 Cr from ₹47.8 Cr…
item.content:encoded:
PharmEasy-backed Thyrocare’s net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) slumped 68.2% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹15.2 Cr from ₹47.8 Cr in the year-ago period. This also marks a 70% dip from ₹51.3 Cr profit in the previous quarter.

The company’s bottom line was weighed by an exceptional impairment loss of about ₹45 Cr on its investment in radiology and diagnostic-imaging subsidiary Nueclear Healthcare Limited (NHL). 

The company’s board approved the sale of its entire stake in the wholly owned subsidiary to Trovera Healthcare for about ₹141.4 Cr on September 21. The impairment costs come at the behest of the definitive term sheet for the proposed sale of the business.

“Thyrocare has issued a postal ballot seeking shareholders’ approval for the proposed divestment of its Nuclear Imaging business, enabling the company to sharpen its focus and allocate capital towards its Pathology business, which offers a stronger growth trajectory, higher margins and better return on capital employed (ROCE),” the company said in a statement.

Meanwhile, the company’s operating revenue rose 25% YoY and 13% QoQ to ₹270.8 Cr in the quarter. In this, revenue from diagnostic testing services rose 26% YoY to ₹256.7 Cr, while revenue from imaging services declined 5% to ₹13.6 Cr.

Including other income of ₹3.6 Cr, total income for the quarter stood at ₹274.4 Cr.

Meanwhile, expenses for the quarter stood at ₹196.6 Cr. Tax expense for the quarter stood at ₹18.4 Cr. 

Without the impairment charge, Thyrocare’s profit before tax spiked about 25% YoY to ₹77.8 Cr. The company’s reported EBITDA for the quarter also increased 25% YoY to ₹89.3 Cr. 

On the operational front, Thyrocare said that it processed 61.6 Mn tests in the quarter, up 27% YoY. The company also said that it worked on further improving its service quality, with customer complaints declining 24% YoY to 2.9 per Mn tests.

Alongside its core pathology business, it is also expanding into specialty diagnostics, starting with allergy testing and genomics. The company entered the genomics business with the launch of non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) and plans to expand its specialty test portfolio.

item.title: Fino Payments Bank Posts ₹21 Cr Loss In Q2, Total Income Falls 17% YoY
item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna
item.description: Fino Payments Bank posted a second consecutive quarter of loss in Q2 FY27, reporting a net loss of ₹20.9 Cr…
item.content:encoded:
Fino Payments Bank posted a second consecutive quarter of loss in Q2 FY27, reporting a net loss of ₹20.9 Cr against a net profit of ₹15.4 Cr in the year-ago period.

This is the second consecutive loss making quarter for the company after the operational disruptions it faced in February. Net loss widened 52.3% from ₹13.7 Cr loss incurred in the previous quarter.  

The company attributed the losses to revenue decline, margin compression and the impact of depreciation. 

“… Profitability dipped due to margin compression and the depreciation impact of our core banking migration. While these investments may pressure short-term earnings, we remain committed to building a resilient and sustainable bank through product innovation, financial discipline, and targeted growth,” said Fino Payments Bank’s interim CFO Anup Agarwal.

The losses came as the company’s total income for the quarter declined 16.6% to ₹333.6 Cr from ₹400.1 Cr in the year-ago quarter. It increased 8.7% from ₹306.9 Cr in the preceding June quarter.

Fino’s other income, which includes fees and commissions from its banking and payment services, declined 23.8% to ₹259.2 Cr from ₹339.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. The company also earned ₹74.5 Cr in interest from investments, balance with RBI and advances in Q2 FY27, up 24% YoY. 

EBITDA tanked 43% to ₹35.1 Cr in Q2 FY27 as against ₹61.6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. The payments bank attributed this to investments in technology, infrastructure, talent and operational capabilities. On similar lines, EBITDA margin also contracted to 10.5% from 15.4% in Q2 FY26.

Meanwhile, Fino’s total expenditure, excluding provisions and contingencies, declined 6.4% YoY to ₹354.5 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹378.8 Cr in Q2 FY26.

In the quarter, the company’s digital payment services business remained non-operational and contributed nil revenue in Q2 FY27. This wiped off a key top line driver. For context, the vertical accounted for 16%, or ₹63.4 Cr, of Fino’s total revenue in the year-ago quarter. It now plans to relaunch the service by Q4 FY27.

Giving a breakdown of its revenue, Fino said that current accounts and savings accounts (CASA) accounted for 52% (₹174 Cr) of its top line in Q2 FY27, while transaction business contributed 17% (₹54.9 Cr). Cash management services contributed another 8% (₹26 Cr) to Fino’s Q2 FY27 revenue.

On the operational front, the payments bank opened 8.2 Lakh new current and savings accounts during the quarter. With this, the total number of CASAs under its belt grew 20% YoY to 19.1 Cr at the end of September 2026. 

As per Fino’s investor presentation, the average total deposits on its platform zoomed 34% YoY to ₹2,490 Cr during the quarter under review. The number of digitally-active customers also rose 13% YoY to 64.9 Lakh in Q2 FY27. 

Overall, Fino processed 92.8 Cr digital transactions during the quarter under review, up 6% YoY, worth ₹64,023 Cr, up 2% YoY. It had also deployed soundboxed at 5,383 merchants at the end of September 2026, which processed payments worth ₹17.3 Cr in Q2 FY27. 

Fino’s loan referral segment, which it sees as a pilot for its proposed small finance bank (SFB), saw disbursals surge 286% YoY to ₹762 Cr, while the number of borrowers rose a marginal 5.5% to 10,467.

On the SFB front, the company said that it has onboarded senior leadership across areas such as branch banking, liabilities, MSME and credit risk. It also claims to be deploying the necessary technology and infrastructure to meet the SFB requirements. 

“The Bank is in (the) consolidation phase and is working towards strengthening its core retail business and restoring growth momentum in B2B businesses. Further, growth in referral loan business is a testimony towards our preparation for future transition and validation of our differentiated SFB model,” said Fino’s interim CEO Ketan Merchant.

Shares of Fino ended Thursday’s trading session 1.03% higher at ₹123.05 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: [Update] Now, Justdial Fined ₹10 Lakh Over Explosive Products Listings
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Update | October 29, 19:45 IST A week after the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) took action against seven ecommerce…
item.content:encoded:
Update | October 29, 19:45 IST

A week after the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) took action against seven ecommerce platforms over listings of unauthorised hazardous explosives, the regulator has now imposed an ₹10 Lakh fine on Justdial.

In an exchange filing today, Justdial said it received an order dated October 28 imposing the penalty for listing and hosting ammonium nitrate, a regulated and hazardous substance, on its platform.

The order also directed the company to immediately remove listings of ammonium nitrate and any other substance classified as an explosive under the Explosives Act, 1884, or other applicable laws.

Justdial said it had discontinued the listings and was reviewing the order. It added that the financial impact would be limited to the penalty amount, with no impact on its operations or other activities.

Original | October 20, 16:42 IST

The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has taken regulatory action against seven ecommerce platforms, including IndiaMART and Justdial, over the listing and sales of unauthorised hazardous explosives.

The material listed on these platforms included ammonium nitrate, gun powder, picric acid and pentaerythritol tetranitrate (PETN).

Except for ammonium nitrate, all of the aforementioned chemicals are exclusively used in manufacturing explosives.

The regulatory action has resulted in the delisting of 3,940 sellers and listing entries, while the authority has imposed penalties totalling ₹30 Lakh on Dial4Trade and ExportersIndia, the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution said in a statement yesterday.

IndiaMART accounted for the highest number of affected sellers and listings, with 3,092, followed by ExportersIndia with 421, Justdial with 206 and TradeIndia with 166, according to the ministry. Other platforms facing regulatory action include Dial4Trade, Sigma-Aldrich India and Ibuychemikals.

In its statement, the consumer protection body shared that it had issued notices to both Justdial and IndiaMART over the listings. Following the notices, Director General – Investigation investigated the matter and shared their reports with the companies. 

IndiaMART submitted its reply to the investigation report and, subsequently, approached the Delhi High Court challenging the SCN issued by the CCPA. Meanwhile, Justdial has sought adjournments in the matter till now and is yet to respond to the investigation. The next and final hearing in the matter is scheduled to be held on October 23.

 Meanwhile, the CCPA has imposed a penalty of ₹10 Lakh on Dial4Trade for facilitating the sale of ammonium nitrate. ExportersIndia was fined ₹10 Lakh in two separate cases, one involving ammonium nitrate and Pentaerythritol Tetranitrate (PETN), and the other involving picric acid.

The CCPA’s action covers both marketplaces that host third-party sellers and platforms that sell products directly. Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals and Ibuychemikals have told the authority that they sell their own products and do not host third-party sellers. Investigations into TradeIndia, Sigma-Aldrich Chemicals and Ibuychemikals are ongoing.

Dial4Trade challenged the order before the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC), which dismissed its appeal on October 9. The commission held that the listings amounted to misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

ExportersIndia has also appealed against the CCPA’s orders before the NCDRC. The appeals are expected to be listed for hearing in the coming period.

Consumers can report listings of explosives on online platforms through the national consumer helpline at 1915.

Under the Explosives Act, 1884, the sale and purchase of these substances require prescribed licences. The CCPA expects platforms to ensure sellers display valid licences issued by the petroleum and explosives safety organisation (PESO) and verify buyers’ identities and licence status before allowing purchases.

“The action reinforces the Government’s commitment to ensuring that digital marketplaces do not facilitate unauthorised access to regulated or dangerous substances in violation of applicable laws and consumer safety standards,” the ministry said.

item.title: Venttup Raises $3 Mn To Bridge India’s Precision Manufacturing Gap
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: For hardware and deeptech startups, the challenge does not end with a working prototype. Moving to commercial production requires manufacturing…
item.content:encoded:
For hardware and deeptech startups, the challenge does not end with a working prototype. Moving to commercial production requires manufacturing partners that can consistently meet technical specifications at scale.

Bengaluru-based Venttup is helping businesses bridge this gap. Founded in 2021 by Sandeep Nair, M. Wasim Ankli, and Joseph Panakkal, the startup combines in-house engineering with a network of manufacturing partners, primarily MSMEs, to support component development, testing, and production.

It has raised $3 Mn in a Pre-Series A round led by Rainmatter by Zerodha and Unicorn India Ventures. The capital will fund engineering hires, precision manufacturing and rapid prototyping infrastructure, and AI adoption for B2B sourcing, supplier intelligence, and operational efficiency.

From Prototypes To Production

Venttup works with original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), technology companies, and deeptech startups, including businesses seeking domestic alternatives to imported components.

Customers can approach it with designs or component requirements. Venttup coordinates engineering, supplier selection and qualification, prototype testing, quality inspections, and production.

Its capabilities span precision machining, casting and forging, sheet metal fabrication, box builds, special purpose machines, industrial automation, and robotics.

“India’s next phase of manufacturing growth requires strong engineering capabilities that can translate complex requirements into validated, production-ready components,” said cofounder and CEO Nair.

“At Venttup, we are building an engineering-first manufacturing startup that brings together design standardisation, rapid prototyping, testing and scalable production through India’s capable MSME ecosystem,” he added.

Venttup operates across four verticals: energy transition and data centres; aerospace, defence, and space systems; smart infrastructure and future mobility; and electronics, automation, and smart manufacturing.

Building A Commercial Base

Incubated at Kerala Startup Mission, Venttup’s founding team brings experience across Hitachi Energy, Siemens, L&T, and Kalpataru Power.

Since its undisclosed seed round in 2024, revenue has grown fivefold to ₹10 Cr in FY26, the startup said. It added more than 15 blue-chip customers over the past 12 months and built an approximately ₹30 Cr business opportunity pipeline across new energy, mobility, and smart infrastructure.

The fresh funding will help the startup expand its manufacturing capabilities and support customers from product development to production.

Venttup’s services overlap with Zetwerk’s precision manufacturing operations and CapGrid’s component sourcing, localisation, and manufacturing services. Karkhana is another peer in taking hardware products into production, with a stronger electronics manufacturing focus.

Inc42 Take: Can Venttup Become More Than A Sourcing Partner?

Venttup’s opportunity lies in taking responsibility for the engineering, validation, and manufacturing work that sits between a component design and commercial production. Its planned Bengaluru facility could give it greater control over this process, while its MSME network offers access to a wider range of manufacturing capabilities.

The test is whether customers see lasting value in keeping Venttup involved once a component is validated and production stabilises. Consistent quality, delivery, and support for subsequent product development will matter more than access to suppliers alone.

Winning repeat production contracts will be the clearest test of whether Venttup can become a long-term manufacturing partner rather than a supplier customers use only during product development.

Trucking platform BlackBuck reported a 41.8% jump in consolidated net profit to ₹41.4 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 from ₹29.2 Cr in the year-ago period.

Operating revenue climbed 55.7% to ₹235.3 Cr from ₹151.1 Cr.

Sequentially, net profit declined 1.8% from ₹42.2 Cr, while operating revenue increased 15.3% from ₹204.2 Cr.

BlackBuck’s profit growth was supported by a sharp reduction in its tax expense to ₹1.4 Cr from ₹9.7 Cr a year earlier. Profit before tax increased 10% YoY to ₹42.8 Cr from ₹38.9 Cr. 

The company recognised a deferred tax credit of ₹1.2 Cr during the quarter as against a deferred tax expense of ₹5.9 Cr in Q2 FY26. Its current tax expense also declined to ₹2.6 Cr from ₹3.9 Cr.

Meanwhile, EBITDA rose 39% YoY to ₹50.6 Cr from ₹36.5 Cr. Adjusted EBITDA, which also excludes employee share-based payment expenses, increased 29% to ₹55 Cr from ₹42.7 Cr.

Other income stood at ₹17.8 Cr, compared with ₹16.1 Cr a year earlier. Including this, total income increased to ₹253.2 Cr from ₹167.2 Cr.

Total expenses rose 64% YoY to ₹210.3 Cr from ₹128.3 Cr, outpacing operating revenue growth.

Growth Businesses Gain Ground

BlackBuck’s core payments and telematics businesses reported a 31% YoY increase in revenue to ₹161.4 Cr from ₹123.4 Cr. Revenue from these businesses grew 11% sequentially.

Its offerings include toll payments through FASTag, fuel payments, vehicle tracking, AIS-GPS devices, and fuel sensors.

The tolling business recorded a 17% YoY increase in gross transaction value (GTV) to ₹7,070 Cr from ₹6,039 Cr. The number of tolling transactions rose 12% to 17.4 Cr.

BlackBuck also reported an increase in FASTag issuances and said its telematics business recorded new highs in device sales.

Meanwhile, revenue from its growth businesses, which include managed freight service Superloads, freight marketplace Loads Classifieds, and vehicle financing, surged 166% YoY to ₹73.9 Cr from ₹27.8 Cr. Revenue increased 25% sequentially.

The company said Superloads’ growth was supported by productivity gains in existing cities and expansion into new markets, while unit economics continued to strengthen.

Its vehicle finance business remained on track to achieve EBITDA break-even, supported by growth in AUM on a steady cost base, it added.

Transacting Customer Base Expands

BlackBuck’s average monthly transacting truck operators increased 13% YoY to 8,95,125 from 7,91,670.

Monthly transacting users using at least two services rose 19% to 4.76 Lakh from 3.99 Lakh. However, average daily time spent on the app by transacting customers declined 3% to 41.8 minutes from 43.2 minutes.

Founded in 2015 by Rajesh Kumar Naidu Yabaji, Chanakya Hridaya, and Ramasubramanian Balasubramaniam, BlackBuck provides digital services to truck operators, spanning payments, vehicle tracking, freight discovery, and vehicle financing. It also operates an online B2B marketplace for intercity full truckload (FTL) transportation.

item.dc:creator: Akshit Pushkarna

item.content:encoded:
Logistics company Shadowfax reported an over 5X year-on-year (YoY) jump in its net profit for the September quarter (Q2 FY27) to ₹68 Cr from ₹13 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, net profit increased 3.9% from ₹65.4 Cr. 

Operating revenue for the quarter surged 57% YoY and 13% QoQ to ₹1,537.7 Cr, a new all-time high in terms of quarterly revenue. Including other income of ₹20.4 Cr, total income for the quarter stood at ₹1,558.1 Cr.

The company said this marked its sixth consecutive quarter of revenue growth exceeding 55% YoY, despite the sale season shifting to Q3 FY27.

Meanwhile, total expenses rose 53% YoY to ₹1,490.2 Cr.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 177.4% YoY to ₹77 Cr, with the corresponding margin expanding to 5% from 2.8%.

“We head into the festive peak with more capacity than ever, and with an AI-led optimisation engine planning our national network every day… Shadowfax expects to remain India’s fastest-growing 3PL while delivering industry-leading returns,” cofounder and CEO Abhishek Bansal said.

Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Bansal and Vaibhav Khandelwal, Shadowfax provides last-mile delivery services to ecommerce platforms and D2C brands. 

The company listed on the stock exchanges in January this year following its ₹1,907 Cr IPO, which included a ₹1,000 Cr fresh issue alongside an offer for sale.

Hyperlocal Revenue Jumps 88%

Shadowfax’s express parcel vertical contributed ₹1,096 Cr in revenue, up 55.2% YoY and 9.9% sequentially.

Revenue from its hyperlocal business grew 87.7% YoY and 25.7% QoQ to ₹341 Cr. Other logistics services contributed ₹100 Cr, up 6.6% YoY and 12.6% sequentially.

The company delivered a combined 27.1 Cr orders across its express parcel and hyperlocal businesses, up 69.7% YoY and 9.8% from the previous quarter.

Express parcel accounted for 21.7 Cr orders, or about 80% of the total, while hyperlocal contributed 5.4 Cr orders.

Small Seller Platform Expands

Shadowfax said its self-serve shipping platform for small sellers, Shadowfax 360, crossed 6,700 transacting sellers within two quarters of launch. Two-thirds joined directly without a salesperson’s involvement.

The company is also launching micro-fulfilment centres for D2C brands and vertical platforms, aiming to enable deliveries within eight to 12 hours without requiring brands to invest in regional warehouses.

Ahead of the festive season, Shadowfax deployed an in-house AI system to plan routes across its national network. The company said the system replans daily how more than 3,600 trucks connect over 5,500 touchpoints.

Shares of Shadowfax were trading nearly 1.3% higher at ₹294.15 on the BSE at 15:25 IST.

item.title: Pine Labs Q2 Profit Jumps Over 6X YoY To ₹38.6 Cr, Revenue Rises 24%
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: Pine Labs’ net profit jumped over 6X year-on-year (YoY) to ₹38.6 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹6 Cr in the…
item.content:encoded:
Pine Labs’ net profit jumped over 6X year-on-year (YoY) to ₹38.6 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹6 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, net profit rose 97% from ₹19.6 Cr in Q1 FY27.

Operating revenue grew 24% YoY and 9% sequentially to ₹806.2 Cr during the quarter. Including other income of ₹25.6 Cr, total income stood at ₹831.7 Cr, up 24% from ₹672.9 Cr in Q2 FY26.

Total expenses rose 16% YoY to ₹770.4 Cr from ₹661.7 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Tax expenses stood at ₹22.8 Cr.

Pine Labs’ adjusted EBITDA rose 27% YoY to ₹215.5 Cr in Q2 FY27, with a margin of 19.2%. Its operating cash flow doubled to ₹350 Cr, while its contribution margin grew 18% YoY to ₹587 Cr. The company had a net cash balance of ₹2,345 Cr as of September 30, 2026.

“Pine Labs has been EBITDA-positive for a long time. We aim to balance investments in new products, ideas and regions while remaining strongly EBITDA-positive. We aim to strike a balance between EBITDA margins of over 20% and revenue growth of 21-23%,” said CEO Amrish Rau.

Pine Labs Sees Growth Across Payments, International Markets

Pine Labs’ two business verticals — digital infrastructure and transaction platform (DITP) & issuing and acquiring platform (AIP) — registered double digit revenue growths in the quarter. DITP’s revenue jumped 21% YoY to ₹440.1 Cr while AIP grew by 30% to ₹274.6 Cr. 

During the quarter, the platform processed around ₹4.45 Lakh Cr ($46.5 Bn) in gross transaction value (GTV) across 229 Cr transactions. Meanwhile, its merchant base grew 13% YoY to 11.6 Lakh, while digital checkout points (DCPs), which include point-of-sale terminals and other merchant payment acceptance solutions, increased 17% to 2.23 Lakh.

More than 29% of Pine Labs’ DITP GTV was monetised through flow-based revenue, affordability and online payments, compared with 15% a year ago. Subscription revenue accounted for 27% of total revenue, while 30% of its DCPs generated flow and affordability GTV.

Pine Labs’ fintech infrastructure business recorded over 33% YoY growth in transactions, with its AI-based credit underwriting platform, SignalIQ, processing more than 1.25 Lakh loans a month.

International markets contributed 15% of Pine Labs’ revenue in Q2 FY27. The company operates in over 22 markets and offers credit processing services in more than 17. Revenue from Southeast Asia grew around 40% YoY, while its DCPs in the region nearly tripled to 1 Lakh. Its UAE business crossed 1 Lakh daily transactions, and the company is expanding in the UAE, the Philippines and Singapore, drawing on its experience in Malaysia.

Pine Labs Sees Meaningful Upside From UPI MDR 

Pine Labs is seeing a “meaningful upside” from the proposed UPI merchant discount rate (MDR) framework, which could allow it to earn fees on eligible merchant transactions above ₹2,000. It noted that more than 70% of its DCP transactions are UPI-led, while transactions above ₹2,000 account for over 65% of its UPI GTV.

“Our average UPI ticket size is ₹1,400 as of Q2 FY27 with more than 65% of our UPI GTV driven by transactions above ₹2,000. Combined with our stronghold in enterprise, mid-market, and premium retail segments, where transactions above ₹2,000 are common, we are well positioned. Under NPCI’s proposed framework, a 0.4% MDR cap applies to payments above ₹2,000, and we primarily expect to earn our proportion through our acquiring bank partners—a high-margin revenue stream that scales with volumes,” the company said in its shareholder letter.

Around three out of every four transactions on Pine Labs’ POS terminals are UPI transactions, with volumes growing at a compounded rate of around 68% over the past two years, CEO Rau said during the company’s Q2 FY27 earnings call. Under the proposed framework, the acquiring bank’s share of the 40 basis points (bps) MDR cap is expected to be around 11 bps, Rau said.

To capture a larger share of the potential revenue, Pine Labs plans to deploy an additional 10 Lakh soundboxes at merchant locations where UPI transactions are currently processed through competitors’ devices.

“There is a large merchant which has POS machines from Pine Labs and soundboxes from somebody else. Those are the things which we have been missing. We said we should take that back,” Rau said.

He added that soundbox deployment had not been a priority earlier because UPI transactions did not generate monetisation opportunities for the company. “Now that it is monetisable, you can get the full wallet share,” he said.

However, Pine Labs will need to hold individual commercial discussions with its largest enterprise clients before passing on the MDR. Rau also remained guarded on the implementation timeline, saying, “I have nothing more to add in terms of when UPI MDR will go live. Now it is completely in NPCI’s court.”

Shares of Pine Labs ended today’s trading 1.03% higher at ₹123.05 apiece on the BSE.

item.title: Freshworks Acquires AI Startup Robusta To Strengthen IT Operations Platform
item.dc:creator: Palak Sharma
item.description: Nasdaq-listed SaaS major Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev for an undisclosed amount to strengthen its IT service…
item.content:encoded:
Nasdaq-listed SaaS major Freshworks has acquired Israel-based AI startup Robusta Dev for an undisclosed amount to strengthen its IT service management platform Freshservice.

The acquisition will add AI-powered capabilities to investigate technology outages, identify their underlying causes, and recommend corrective actions. Freshworks plans to integrate these capabilities into Freshservice and deepen their interoperability with incident response platforms such as FireHydrant.

Founded by Natan Yellin and Arik Alon, Robusta uses AI agents to analyse monitoring data, information from IT infrastructure, and recent code or configuration changes to determine what caused an outage. It also identifies how disruptions affect connected services and recommends steps to resolve them.

According to Freshworks, the technology is designed to reduce manual investigations, consolidate alerts, and help engineering teams resolve incidents faster. Engineers can review and approve recommended actions before changes are made to production systems.

“Our technology lets AI Agents do that effectively in large enterprise environments, where there are so many raw events that investigating each one individually would be exorbitant from a token cost perspective. We’re incredibly excited to join Freshworks, which gives us the scale and platform to bring that experience to engineering teams everywhere, while keeping humans firmly in control of decisions that touch production,” said Robusta founder Yellin.

Freshworks said the integration would connect incident diagnosis, response, and prevention workflows, helping businesses use findings from earlier outages to reduce recurring disruptions.

The deal expands Freshworks’ AI-powered service operations offerings, which focus on automating IT workflows and helping enterprises manage technology incidents.

Founded in 2010 by Girish Mathrubootham and Shanmugam Krishnasamy, Freshworks offers cloud-based software for customer engagement, sales, and IT service management.

The Robusta deal follows Freshworks’ agreement to acquire Torii, announced earlier this month. The SaaS management platform helps enterprises track software usage and govern AI spending.

The company also acquired US-based incident management startup FireHydrant in Demember last year. While FireHydrant helps enterprises coordinate responses to software outages, Robusta adds AI-powered root-cause analysis and remediation recommendations. 

On the financial front, Freshworks reported a $4.8 Mn net loss for Q1 2026, even as revenue grew 16% YoY to $228.6 Mn. It also announced plans to cut around 11% of its workforce, or approximately 500 employees, as it sought to increase the use of AI in product development and automate routine work.

item.title: Ace Blend Raises $9.9 Mn To Fund Clinical Trials, Expand Nutrition Portfolio
item.dc:creator: Shrishti Bisht
item.description: D2C nutrition and dietary supplements brand Ace Blend has raised $9.9 Mn (about ₹95 Cr) in a Series A2 funding…
item.content:encoded:
D2C nutrition and dietary supplements brand Ace Blend has raised $9.9 Mn (about ₹95 Cr) in a Series A2 funding round led by 3one4 Capital, with participation from existing investor Fireside Ventures.

The startup will use the fresh capital for clinical trials, supply chain improvements, R&D, and new nutrition formats.

“The first is clinical trials, which are going to be run by credible CROs (contract research organisations) and are intended to be published in peer-reviewed international journals. The second is cementing our moat as a business, which is our supply chain proficiency. The third is a robust testing mechanism that allows nutritional accuracy, pesticides and heavy metals to be tested batch on batch without any human intervention,” founder and CEO Shivam Hingorani told Inc42.

Ace Blend also plans to conduct shelf-stability studies at launch and six months later, which Hingorani said would help build long-term safety data on its products.

“Trust is not enough” in the nutritional supplements market, he said, stressing the need for scientific evidence to support product claims.

Founded in 2018 by Hingorani, and later joined by Saif Mehkri as cofounder in 2022, Ace Blend offers supplements across heart health, brain health, sleep, recovery, gut health, strength and immunity. Its portfolio comprises around 14 SKUs, including plant-based protein powders, superfood mixes, and functional health supplements.

Besides its website, the startup sells its products through ecommerce and quick commerce platforms, including Amazon, Flipkart, Zepto, and Blinkit. Its website contributes around 50% of revenue, with the remainder coming from marketplaces and other ecommerce channels, Hingorani said.

Ace Blend clocked 300% growth in FY26 and has a repeat purchase rate of nearly 48%, according to Hingorani. It is targeting annual recurring revenue of ₹250-300 Cr over the next 12-18 months, with profitability also in sight, he added.

The startup plans to strengthen its supply chain by sourcing raw materials from multiple countries. Hingorani said its vertically integrated model covers ingredient sourcing, formulation, and manufacturing, while automated testing will assess nutritional accuracy, pesticide residues, and heavy metals in each batch.

Ace Blend is also developing new products, including a formulation created with a gut-health specialist to address leaky gut, a combination of natural nutrients intended to lower inflammation, an eye-health product, and a fibre-based format for gut health, he said.

India’s dietary supplements market is growing as consumers become more aware of preventive healthcare and the role of supplements in managing chronic conditions. Investor interest in the sector is also rising. Earlier this month, D2C brand The Stack raised ₹21.5 Cr to expand its product range and invest in R&D.

According to Grand View Research, India’s dietary supplements market was valued at $5.8 Bn in 2025. It is projected to reach $6.6 Bn in 2026 and $12.4 Bn by 2033, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9.5% between 2026 and 2033.

item.title: Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026: What’s In Store For Startups At Asia’s Largest Tech Event

item.content:encoded:
India’s startup ecosystem is the fourth most valuable startup ecosystem in the world and spans from fintech and consumer technology to AI and deeptech sectors. As founders look beyond domestic markets to build globally competitive businesses, access to capital, talent and technology infrastructure has become increasingly important.

Bengaluru has long brought these ingredients together. For close to three decades, the Silicon Valley of India has been the yardstick against which India’s tech ambitions are measured. The city now ranks 15th among global startup ecosystems and 12th among the world’s largest tech talent hubs.

Meanwhile, Karnataka accounts for 42% of India’s IT exports and leads the country in software exports, biotech, and aerospace and defence manufacturing.

As AI changes how products are developed and businesses operate, the opportunity is expanding – build from Bengaluru and reach the world.

This ambition will take centre stage at the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) 2026. Organised by the Karnataka government’s Department of Electronics, Information Technology, Biotechnology and Science & Technology, the Summit returns for its 29th edition from November 17-19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC), Bengaluru.

Under the theme ‘AI & Beyond’, the three-day event will bring together founders, investors, technology leaders, researchers, and policymakers to explore emerging technologies and the businesses being built around them.

Billed as Asia’s largest integrated technology event, BTS 2026 expects more than 60K business visitors, over 25K delegates, 1,800+ exhibitors and 700+ speakers across 120+ sessions. 

Participation is expected from over 75 countries and 30+ Indian states and Union Territories. It will also feature more than 20 country pavilions and over 175 international exhibitors on the floor.

The summit will span 18 thematic tracks, covering IT and deeptech, frontier technologies, electronics and semiconductors, electric mobility, health and biotech, data centres, cybersecurity, global capability centres (GCCs), fintech, and the orange economy, which encompasses creative industries. A dedicated India-USA Tech Conclave will also be part of the programme.

The speaker line-up announced so far includes Sandeep Sahai, chief executive officer, Clear Water Analytics, Vivek Raghavan, cofounder, Sarvam AI, Dr V. Anantha Nageswaran, chief economic advisor (CEA), Govt. of India, Ranjani Mani, director and country head – generative AI, Microsoft, Rangesh Raghavan, corporate vice president and MD, Lam Research, Dr Sowmya Swaminathan, chairperson, M S Swaminathan Research Foundation, and Dr Velislava Petrova-Chamova, minister of foreign affairs of the Republic of Bulgaria. 

For founders, the programme extends beyond conference sessions to product showcases, investor meetings, and practical guidance on building and scaling businesses.

A Global Startup Showcase 

The Startup Pavilion will host more than 1,000 startups, incubators, and accelerators, with startup participation spanning 100 cities. These will include cohorts from the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission’s (KDEM) ‘Beyond Bengaluru’ initiative and the Software Technology Parks of India’s ‘Sayuj’ programme.

Eighteen thematic pavilions will cover sectors including AI, agritech, D2C, fintech, semiconductors, robotics, and SaaS. By grouping startups within their industry segments, the exhibition aims to help founders connect with relevant buyers, customers, and potential partners.

Two dedicated startup stages will focus on ‘Deeptech For Business’ and ‘Consumer Tech For Billions’. Both stages will host workshops and masterclasses on topics such as go-to-market strategies, investor readiness, product management, cybersecurity and AI.

Connecting Founders With Investors 

On the sidelines of BTS 2026, the three-day ‘Investor Connect Programme’ will offer curated, sector-specific matchmaking between startups, investors, and corporates. At the pitching arena, tech founders will get a shot at presenting to global VCs. 

The three-day initiative is shaped in a way to bring startups face-to-face with investors, corporates, and key ecosystem stakeholders who can unlock collaborative projects, build investor relationships and connect young businesses with potential customers.

The programme will also host a reverse pitching session that will turn the tables, with investors explaining their investment theses, portfolio focus, and the businesses they want to back. Startups will also have access to one-on-one mentoring sessions with entrepreneurs, investors, policymakers and domain experts. 

Celebrating India’s Future Makers

Another addition to the broader BTS 2026 umbrella is the Future Makers Conclave, a platform to celebrate India’s next generation of innovators and entrepreneurs. The conclave will bring together founders, entrepreneurs, investors and thought leaders to exchange ideas, share experiences, and discuss emerging opportunities across the technology and startup ecosystem.

The day will feature the BTS Unicorn Felicitation, where the state government will honour Indian startups that have entered the unicorn club since the previous edition. The conclave will also mark 10 years of the Karnataka government’s Elevate programme, which supports startups in the state.

The Bengaluru Tech Summit will also host key industry players, including Infosys, Biocon, QpiAI, Bosch Global Software Technologies, Clearwater Analytics, Booking Holdings, ZS, SAP, eBay, ACT Enterprise, Applied Materials, Fujitsu Ltd, Cloudflare, Qualcomm, Intel, JetBrains, Antithesis, PLAUD, Kyndle IT and many more as sponsors, alongside international partners like Business Sweden, Italian Trade Agency, Australian Trade & Investment Commission, Poland and more. 

Together, the startup exhibition, investor programmes, and the Future Makers Conclave aim to make BTS 2026 a meeting point for ideas, capital, and commercial opportunities – giving founders a platform to take their next step towards global growth.

item.title: Kissht Q2: Profit Doubles To ₹125 Cr, Revenue Jumps 45% YoY
item.dc:creator: Vinaykumar Rai
item.description: Lending tech platform Kissht’s parent OnEMI Technology Solutions reported a 100.4% jump in consolidated net profit to ₹125.1 Cr in…
item.content:encoded:
Lending tech platform Kissht’s parent OnEMI Technology Solutions reported a 100.4% jump in consolidated net profit to ₹125.1 Cr in the September quarter of FY27 from ₹62.4 Cr a year earlier.

Operating revenue climbed 44.7% to ₹731.8 Cr during the quarter under review from ₹505.7 Cr in Q2 FY26. 

On a sequential basis, net profit grew 31.6% from ₹95.1 Cr, while operating revenue rose 9.3% from ₹669.5 Cr.

Including other income of ₹8.5 Cr, Kissht’s total income stood at ₹740.3 Cr in Q2 FY27.

Total expenses increased 34.9% YoY to ₹586 Cr from ₹434.5 Cr. The company’s pre-provision operating profit, which excludes impairment costs and tax, rose 39.9% YoY to ₹287 Cr from ₹205 Cr.

Founded in 2015 by Ranvir Singh and Krishnan Vishwanathan, Kissht offers digital lending products, including personal loans and loans against property (LAP). Its group includes lending subsidiary Si Creva Capital Services.

Kissht’s assets under management (AUM) grew 68% YoY and 16% sequentially to ₹9,317 Cr at the end of September 2026, driven by continued expansion of its lending portfolio.

Personal loans accounted for ₹8,580 Cr, or 92.1% of AUM, while LAP contributed ₹737 Cr, or 7.9%.
Off-book loans, originated through arrangements with partner lenders, accounted for ₹5,118 Cr, or 54.9% of total AUM. Kissht had more than 45 active lending and co-lending partners at the end of the September quarter.

The company said it had served 12.8 Mn customers cumulatively, including 3.61 Mn active customers, at the end of the quarter. Its LAP business operated through 107 branches across nine states and Union Territories.

Total loan disbursements rose 55.7% YoY to ₹4,611.5 Cr. Disbursements also increased 21% sequentially from ₹3,811.9 Cr in Q1 FY27.

The average ticket size of loans disbursed increased 84.7% YoY to ₹43,377, while average loan tenure rose 43% to 17.8 months from 12.45 months.

Self-employed borrowers accounted for 54.7% of customers. 

Kissht’s Asset Quality Improves

Kissht’s gross non-performing asset (GNPA) ratio declined to 2.18% from 2.93% a year earlier and 2.25% in the June quarter. Net NPA ratio stood at 0.34% as against 0.36% in Q1 FY27. The provision coverage ratio, which measures provisions against gross bad loans, was 84.55%.

Collection efficiency for loans up to 30 days past due (DPD) stood at 97.12% during the quarter.

The lender attributed its performance to its underwriting and risk management systems, including the use of AI and machine learning in credit decisioning, fraud detection, and collections.

“Our priorities remain unchanged: to grow sustainably without compromising credit quality and to deliver consistent, profitable returns over the long term,” chairman, director, and CEO Singh said.

For FY27, Kissht raised its AUM growth guidance to over 60% from over 40%. It also guided for a reduction of more than 15% YoY in credit costs as against 10-15% earlier.

The company maintained its GNPA target at below 2.25% and revised its return on average equity (RoAE) guidance to over 20% from a range of 19-21%. 

Alongside the results, Kissht’s board approved a ₹624.1 Cr investment in wholly owned subsidiary Si Creva through a rights issue.

The investment will use at least 75% of the proceeds from its ₹832.2 Cr preferential issue to strengthen the subsidiary’s capital base for business growth. The infusion is expected to be completed by the end of December.
